name: IWE presents: Back From the Dead

date.source: The federation's own comeback broadcast, posted three days late by its own account on 2 July 2003, itself billed for Saturday, 28 June 2003 ("On June 28th Chicago will be ablaze once more").

evidence.source: IWE presents: Back From the Dead (full broadcast transcript), posted 2 July 2003
evidence.note: The sole primary source for this record: a full-card comeback special, including a pre-show hype package, ring announcements, and a trailing match-writer credit block.

matches.note: Opening contest. Both men tumbled together over the top rope to the floor and were counted out simultaneously; ruled a draw. A post-bell brawl continued until IWE security separated them.

matches.stipulation: AeWF Television Championship, career-vs-title match (loser's in-ring career ends)
matches.note: Rune pinned the defending champion, King Snake, after kicking out of two Snake Bites, to win the title; per the match's own stipulation, King Snake's in-ring career ended with the loss. A six-years-in-the-making grudge, per the broadcast's own commentary.

matches.stipulation: IWE World Tag Team Championship, four-way elimination match (newly reinstated titles)

eliminations.note: Karma pinned Steven with a shooting star press into a DDT ("Nicotine").

Atkins pinned Jeremy Bishop moments after Lyell Jett flattened partner Richard Sheridan with the Fertigig Krieg; the announcers named the fallen team the promotion's own former IWE World Tag Team Champions.
Atkins hit a top-rope Shooting Star Press to pin Karma moments after an unseen chairshot; K. Ashe Adams' save attempt was cut off by Lyell Jett.

matches.note: Enemies of the State won the newly reinstated titles. Immediately after, the previously unannounced High Stakes Gamblers (Shawn Montgomery and an unnamed partner) ran in with a pool stick and a cattle brand, beat down all three losing teams and the new champions, claimed to be the reigning KAWF World Tag Team Champions newly signed to IWE, and issued an open challenge.

matches.stipulation: Windy City Skyscraper scaffold match (retrieve the flag atop a thirty-foot scaffold to win)
matches.note: Both men fought through the arena and onto the scaffold; Robinson's leap for the flag was followed by both men crashing through a stack of tables below. Williams was blown from the scaffold by a gust of wind before he could reach the flag; Robinson, though bloodied, refused medical attention, climbed back up, and retrieved it to win.

matches.stipulation: IWE Intercontinental Championship (vacant four years), two out of three falls, each man choosing one fall's stipulation and the promotion's owner choosing the third
matches.note: Fall one: a Cactus and Scorpion Deathmatch (the Outlaw's choice), won by the Outlaw with a spinebuster off the top rope. Fall two: a Flaming Table Match (Maxwell's choice), won by Maxwell. Fall three: a steel cage match (chosen by the promotion's own owner); after both men traded turnbuckle dives (the Outlaw setting Maxwell's face on fire with one), the Outlaw climbed down to the floor to win the match and the vacant title.

A respect-driven exhibition with no title on the line; Langston Crete won by a surprise backslide, an upset the broadcast's own commentary called it. Sabbath raised the rookie's arm himself afterward.

matches.stipulation: Ladder match for the number-one contendership to the IWE World Heavyweight Championship
matches.note: Setzer Van Strife, wrestling in his hometown, retrieved the contract off the ladder to win. Eric Cooper refused a stretcher and walked out under his own power.

matches.stipulation: vacant IWE World Heavyweight Championship, one fall (title vacant since the promotion's 1999 closure)
matches.note: Main event. Dante Reid had controversially replaced an earlier elimination to join the match; Brian Floyd had secretly paid the new tag champions, Enemies of the State, to take Reid out. Enemies of the State ran in during the match's final stretch, powerbombed Reid, then hurled Floyd himself over the top rope to the concrete, revealing they had taken Floyd's money only to double-cross him too. Johnny Malibu pinned the prone Dante Reid with the Glamour Bomb to win the vacant title, then, in the show's closing act of cruelty, invited Floyd's manager Knee High into the ring to celebrate and planted him with the Glamour Bomb as well.

notes: A ninth match advertised in the show's own pre-show hype package -- a "special midget match" between Knee High and Mini Neige -- is explicitly announced mid-broadcast as postponed to a future show ("Mini Neige will take on Knee High at the new IWE show, Sunday Night Showcase") and is not structured here as a result on this card. The broadcast closes with an angle, not a match: original founder Jay Ralston interrupts the new champion's celebration to reveal he has secretly owned the company all along behind a front man, on-screen IWE Owner Tony Capri, whom he fires for disobeying orders (allowing Dante Reid into the main event, and permitting interference) and has Enemies of the State and Johnny Malibu assault on camera to close the show.
